title: Who Wins the Midterms & What It Means for Markets with Dan Clifton | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 67
summary: Dan Clifton links midterms, tariffs, fiscal stimulus and Fed balance-sheet reform to markets. He expects a Democratic House but leans against a Senate takeover, emphasizes an underpriced data-center backlash and favors defense technology. Eisman challenges the moderate-Democrat scenario and expects a prolonged Iran conflict. Several long-term forecasts remain open; election outcomes require primary tally confirmation. The Supreme Court tariff ruling is verified, while causal macro and political explanations remain substantially unresolved.
assessment: Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts the episode; guest turns are inferred from introductions and conversational context.
framework_points: Use institutional control and budget leverage, not just election labels.
Track the change in fiscal/tariff impulse rather than gross tariff announcements.
Distinguish speculative motives from observable policy.
Treat data-center local costs and tax benefits together.
tools_and_charts: Fed balance sheet and bank deposits
transcript_cautions: Captions confuse Warsh with Walsh and IEEPA with IAPA.
Several recorded timing references precede the July publication date.
Opening and closing summaries repeat guest views; summaries are not automatic host endorsement.
Eisman corrects 2028 to 2026 during a midterm discussion.
Election horizons have passed by the audit cutoff; missing official evidence means unresolved, not too early.
